transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-11-18
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 53 minutes
Attendees: Alex Garner (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Jane Lopez (CTO - Helios), Mark DeVries (Head of Infosec), Samir Khan (Platform Eng), Lena Ortiz (PM)

Summary (auto): quick infosec intake for hosted vs dedicated vs private; main asks: SOC2/ISO posture, SSO/SAML & SCIM, RBAC model, audit logs retention, KMS integration, data residency and retention windows. Agreed next step: share artifacts and schedule infra deep-dive + 1-week POC.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00:05] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is Alex from Redwood, also with Priya, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:00:14] Jane: Good, morning — afternoon I guess, yeah thanks for fitting us in. We wanted to do a quick intake before the procurement folks get noisy.
[00:00:22] Mark: Hi, Mark here. High level: we need to understand the security posture if we use Hosted versus Dedicated versus Private. Our legal team insists on SOC 2 and has a list of questions re key management and data retention.
[00:00:35] Priya: Totally, Mark. We'll walk through what Redwood supports, typical enterprise controls, and where there are trade-offs. I'll jump in with more infra detail as needed.
[00:00:45] Samir: Quick note from infra: we have strict network egress rules and want to avoid putting raw PII out to third party unless it's encrypted and KMS-managed.
[00:00:55] Alex: Understood. At a high level: Redwood Hosted is the fastest to get started — it's our multi-tenant hosted API, SOC2 Type II audited, we have an ISO summary as well. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools for performance and isolation, and Private is a customer-controlled control plane (VPC / on-prem) if you need full network isolation.
[00:01:12] Mark: When you say SOC2 Type II, can we get the actual report or an attestation? Our compliance team wants the report and the scope — e.g., which data flows were in scope, retention of logs, and any subprocessor list.
[00:01:28] Alex: Yes, we can share the SOC2 Type II attestation and a SOC2 summary that lists scope and subprocessors. I'll attach it to the CRM.
[00:01:37] Jane: Also ISO — are you certified or do you have an ISO summary?
[00:01:42] Priya: We have an ISO 27001 summary and control mappings; we aren't audited as large clouds are, but we publish our control mapping for customers.
[00:01:51] Mark: Okay. For SSO — we run enterprise SAML via Okta. Do you support SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning?
[00:01:59] Alex: Yes, SAML SSO supported; SCIM provisioning for user sync is available for Dedicated and Private customers today; for Hosted we support SAML and can integrate with SCIM for teams with enterprise plans.
[00:02:10] Mark: How granular is RBAC? We need role separation between devs, ops, and auditors.
[00:02:15] Priya: RBAC is role-based with custom roles — you can limit token creation, model access, and console actions. Audit logs record who requested tokens and policy changes. For real auditors, we can export logs to your SIEM via syslog / Kinesis or S3 delivery depending on hosting mode.
[00:02:33] Samir: Do audit logs include per-request metadata? We need timestamp, token id, model used, prompt hash — something that helps correlate.
[00:02:41] Priya: Yes, basic request-level metadata is captured: request ID, timestamp, model id, token usage. Prompt text is redacted by default in Hosted; for Dedicated/Private you can opt-in for logging raw payloads but that has data residency implications.
[00:02:56] Mark: What's your default retention? Our policy is 13 months for audit logs.
[00:03:02] Alex: Default retention on Hosted is 90 days for request logs; we offer extended retention add-ons and for Dedicated/Private customers you can configure retention and export to your storage.
[00:03:12] Jane: Encryption — do you manage keys or can we bring our own KMS?
[00:03:16] Priya: Both. Hosted uses Redwood-managed KMS by default, and we provide an option for BYOK with cloud KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure KeyVault) for Dedicated and Private. On Private you can use customer HSMs as well.
[00:03:30] Mark: Any details around key lifecycles and rotation?
[00:03:33] Priya: Rotation is supported — we have key rotation pipelines and you can rotate keys on your schedule with BYOK. We'll provide the key rotation docs.
[00:03:40] Samir: Network — if we go Dedicated in your cloud, do you support VPC peering or private link?
[00:03:46] Alex: Yes, Dedicated supports VPC peering and PrivateLink-like setups depending on cloud. Private gives you full VPC control with customer-managed routing. We'll share the VPC peering guide.
[00:03:57] Mark: What about data at rest — is model cache or KV cache considered persisted customer data? We need to know if anything can leak.
[00:04:05] Priya: Good question. We treat KV cache contents as ephemeral by default, but you can configure cache persistence. For sensitive workloads we recommend Private with encrypted NVMe and customer-managed keys.
[00:04:20] Lena: From product — our usage pattern is a mix of short chat sessions and batch embedding jobs for search reindexing. Latency matters for chat, cost for embeddings. How do I communicate that to you for model recommendations?
[00:04:33] Priya: Send us your expected QPS, average sequence length, and embedding batch sizes. We'll propose quantization and batching profiles and whether Dedicated pool makes sense. For the POC, we can run a representative benchmark.
[00:04:45] Samir: About PII: are there options for token-level masking or redaction before logs are stored?
[00:04:51] Priya: We support configurable redaction rules and post-processing hooks. Hosted has built-in redaction heuristics; Dedicated/Private can plug in your redaction step in the pipeline.
[00:05:05] Mark: Can you sign a DPA with data residency guarantees? We need EU data residency for EEA customers.
[00:05:12] Alex: Yes, we have DPAs and data processing addenda for customers. For EU residency we'd recommend Dedicated in the EU region or Private deployment. We'll surface the legal templates.
[00:05:23] Jane: What about uptime and SLA?
[00:05:27] Alex: Hosted has a best-effort SLA for free tiers, enterprise plans have uptime SLAs for Dedicated. Private SLAs are part of the enterprise agreement. We'll put the SLA table in the doc we share.
[00:05:38] Mark: Are you able to run third-party penetration tests and share results?
[00:05:43] Priya: We run internal pentests and will share summaries; for Dedicated/Private we can coordinate scoping with your security team for an allowed test window. Full pentest reports are sensitive, but we provide redacted summaries and remediation timelines.
[00:05:58] Jane: Any known limitations on inbound/outbound IP whitelisting?
[00:06:03] Alex: IP allow lists are supported for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted, we have API token-based access and support workspace-level allow lists on enterprise plans.
[00:06:12] Mark: For SSO provisioning — can we map groups to roles automatically?
[00:06:17] Priya: Yes, SCIM group to role mappings are supported for enterprise provisioning flows.
[00:06:22] Lena: On the timeline — if we want a POC in December and procurement in January, what do you typically need?
[00:06:29] Alex: We'll need expected workload profile, a list of test prompts or embeddings corpus (anonymized if sensitive), and network allow lists. We'll set up a Dedicated pool for the POC if you want isolated capacity. That aligns with a December POC and Jan procurement.
[00:06:43] Mark: Costs — Dedicated sounds pricey, will it cost 2-3x Hosted?
[00:06:49] Alex: It can be higher on base commit, but unit token cost can be lower because of caching and predictable batching. We'll model the economics once we have your profile.
[00:06:59] Samir: How do rollouts and fallbacks work — e.g. if a model degrades, can we automatically fail back to another variant?
[00:07:06] Priya: Yes, our console supports rollout policies and automatic fallback to pinned model variants or a cheaper fallback. Also you can configure latency SLOs for routing.
[00:07:17] Jane: On auditability — we need immutable logs for a 13-month window and ability to export to our SIEM. Is that supported?
[00:07:25] Priya: Yes — Dedicated/Private can export logs to S3/Kinesis or push to your SIEM; for Hosted we offer log export options and archive add-ons for longer retention.
[00:07:37] Mark: A few technical nitpicks: do you support FIPS endpoints for crypto?
[00:07:42] Alex: FIPS endpoints are available for Dedicated/Private customers using BYOK and the appropriate cloud region; we'll confirm exact coverage per cloud provider.
[00:07:53] Samir: For the POC, we'll need a simple checklist: network, keys, tokens, sample traffic pattern and a runbook to collect metrics.
[00:08:02] Priya: We'll produce a 1-page POC runbook and a longer infra checklist. I'll draft it after this call.
[00:08:09] Mark: What about irreversible deletion? If we want prompt data purged, can you do that?
[00:08:14] Priya: For Hosted we can submit deletion requests and purge logs according to retention; for Dedicated/Private customers with BYOK you can rotate or destroy keys to make on-disk data unrecoverable — we'll explain the process.
[00:08:26] Jane: Any gotchas about model caching that could store data beyond request lifetime?
[00:08:30] Priya: Cache can persist depending on config; by default it's ephemeral and TTL-based. For regulated data we recommend disabling persistence or using Private where you control storage.
[00:08:41] Alex: Alright, quick recap and proposed actions: we'll share SOC 2 and ISO summaries, VPC peering & BYOK docs, and a draft POC runbook. Priya will follow up to schedule the infra deep-dive. Samir will send QPS and example payloads. Mark to confirm retention and legal constraints.
[00:09:01] Mark: That sounds fine. One question from legal side: do you maintain an access log for administration actions in the console?
[00:09:08] Priya: Yes, admin actions are logged and we can provide an audit trail of changes, user grants, and key rotations.
[00:09:16] Jane: Great. If we like the POC, how long is typical procurement lead time?
[00:09:21] Alex: For Dedicated it's typically 6–8 weeks after procurement kickoff; Hosted is faster. We'll support with a procurement packet.
[00:09:31] Samir: On credentials: does Redwood issue long-lived API keys or short-lived tokens? We prefer short-lived with rotation where possible.
[00:09:38] Priya: Short-lived tokens by default; API keys can be issued for service accounts with rotation policies. We also support ephemeral tokens via OIDC flows.
[00:09:49] Mark: Any customer references in retail space we can call?
[00:09:53] Alex: We can provide a couple of anonymized references in retail and logistics — I'll include contact windows.
[00:10:00] Lena: Thanks — that's helpful.
[00:10:03] Alex: Great. Anything else before we wrap?
[00:10:06] Mark: One last: do you have a standard DLP playbook? We need to know how you handle exfil attempts and alerting.
[00:10:13] Priya: We have DLP patterns, anomaly detection for token usage spikes and automated alerting; for Dedicated/Private we can forward alerts to your SOC. We'll send an overview doc.
[00:10:25] Alex: Okay, we'll get those artifacts out. Expect SOC2 + ISO summary, VPC/BYOK docs, POC runbook, and proposed POC dates.
[00:10:32] Jane: Thanks everyone. We'll review and aim to get you the payload and QPS numbers by Friday.
[00:10:38] Alex: Perfect, we'll follow up in CRM and set up the next call. Thanks for your time.
[00:10:43] Mark: Thanks.
[00:10:44] Samir: Thanks all.
